subject: data size from R to shiny app

messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: data size from R to shiny app
parts:
Hi all,

Below you can find a screen capture from a shiny app that I'm building (I think you'll like what you'll see):
http://goo.gl/fHG4w5

For particular reasons, I've chosen an HTML + Javascript approach for the user interface. I would be curious if something like that can be done via shiny directly, but I guess this is just too customised.
However, this is indeed a shiny app because the result on the screen is based on the webpage communicating with R via shiny.

Now about the subject of this email: when displaying the data (especially visible after setting the row.names argument), you can notice a 250ms delay that I determined are necessary for R to observe() the change in the Javascript object, then apply the read.csv() function and return the result back to Javascript.

250ms is not such a bad deal, but this is a very small dataset. I've tries with a larger one... and nothing. It seems that for larger(ish) datasets (for example 1000 rows and 300 columns) something happens with the communication between R and Javascript.

Could anyone point me to some kind of a possible solution?
I know there are shiny tables available, but I kind of like my data editor. Just curious how much data can I fit in this little tool.

Ideally, what I would like to achieve is a rich, highly interactive (and reactive) user interface that would be almost similar to any program installed on a local computer... and that would also imply editing a "normal" sized dataset.

Thanks,
Adrian
